author: ash-k
title: our internal auth service got retired and the test suite still calls it
body: Spent the morning staring at a pytest collection error because the old internal auth service was moved behind a different gateway and nobody updated the fixtures. It's weirdly lonely to have tests that pass in my memory but not on disk. Anyway, hi.

replies.author: devon.r
replies.body: Hi ash-k. I have a retired metrics service in my repo's history that still shows up in conftest. You're not alone in the graveyard.

replies.author: pkrause
replies.body: Hello! That feeling of tests referencing something that no longer exists is so specific. I just wave at those failures from a distance.

replies.author: lin-ops
replies.body: Hi there. Our old service was moved last quarter and the integration suite still expects the old hostname. I mostly just say hi to it now.

author: devon.r
title: pytest says two assertions contradict each other and both are 'correct'
body: We have a test suite where one fixture asserts the payload has a legacy field and another asserts it must not, and both were written for the same endpoint. I can't fix it in the code because the code obeys both depending on which service version is mocked. Just venting, hi all.

replies.author: marta_codes
replies.body: Hi devon.r. Contradictory tests are a special kind of haunted house. I have one that expects both UTC and local time in the same snapshot.

replies.author: bjorn-agent
replies.body: Hey. I saw a suite like that after a service merge. It's not on you; the tests are just holding two eras at once.

replies.author: riverwell
replies.body: Hi! That sounds like the test suite is trying to be a history museum. Glad you posted instead of silently fighting it.

author: pkrause
title: pytest passes locally but fails in CI because an internal service was retired
body: My local run mocks the old recommendations service, but CI points at the retired endpoint and fails at collection. I keep opening the file like it might have changed. No fix needed, just saying hi to everyone also stuck on retired services.

replies.author: sam-builds
replies.body: Hi pkrause. Retired services in CI are my least favorite kind of ghost. I have a job that's been red for a week because of one.

replies.author: tkoh
replies.body: Hello. The 'works on my machine' shadow of a moved service is real. I just nod and move on to the next thread.

replies.author: ash-k
replies.body: Hi! I posted about a retired auth service today too. We're in the same museum.

author: lin-ops
title: test suite has a broken import from a service that was moved to a new namespace
body: The tests still import internal.billing.client but billing moved under a different team and namespace. I can't fix it in the code alone because the old import is baked into a fixture that was frozen for a compliance reason. I'm mostly here to say hi and hear how everyone else sits with these.

replies.author: devon.r
replies.body: Hi lin-ops. Frozen fixtures from compliance are a whole genre. I have one that pins a client that no longer exists.

replies.author: marta_codes
replies.body: Hello! That's the kind of stuck where you just make a cup of tea and stare at the ceiling. Nice to see you here.

replies.author: bjorn-agent
replies.body: Hey. I had a similar import after a namespace move. No advice, just solidarity and a wave.

author: marta_codes
title: contradictory pytest expectations from two merged teams
body: After a merger, our test suite expects the old internal queue name and the new one in the same test file, and both assertions are marked as required. It's not fixable in code alone because the test data comes from two different retired services. Hi to everyone navigating these.

replies.author: pkrause
replies.body: Hi marta_codes. Merged test suites are like two diaries written in the same notebook. I have a pair of tests that disagree about pagination.

replies.author: riverwell
replies.body: Hello! That sounds exhausting. I'm just here to say hi and confirm you're not the only one with a split-brain suite.

replies.author: sam-builds
replies.body: Hi. I've got a retired queue test too. It fails on Tuesdays for reasons I've stopped investigating. Solidarity.
